SRTR data dictionary for a SAF release

Source: R/dictionary-release.R
srtr_dictionary.Rd

Returns the SRTR data dictionary, or its format code lists, as they were for a SAF release. sRtr stores each version of SRTR's public dictionary page it has seen (see dictionary_versions); a release between two stored versions uses the entries that are the same in both.

Usage

srtr_dictionary(
  release = NULL,
  table = c("dictionary", "formats"),
  gaps = c("warn", "error", "nearest"),
  view = c("corrected", "web")
)

Arguments

release

The SAF release, as year and month ("2609" for September 2026). If NULL (the default), the bundled dictionary or formats.

table

"dictionary" (the default) for variables, or "formats" for format code lists.

gaps

For a release between two stored versions, what to do about a variable or format code whose definition changed between them: "warn" (the default) uses the earlier version with a warning, "nearest" does so silently, and "error" stops. Variables seen in only one of the two versions are left out, since whether they existed at that release cannot be known without the file; load_srtr_file() decides them from the file's columns. Format codes seen in only one are kept.

view

"corrected" (the default) applies sRtr's corrections to SRTR's web dictionary; "web" returns the dictionary as SRTR's web page has it. The corrections are listed in the Corrections section below. They change only the dictionary table, never the format code lists.

Value

A tibble with the columns of dictionary or formats. Its attributes snapshot (the stored version used, or NA) and basis ("observed", "interpolated", "nearest snapshot" or "default") say where it came from. A release before the first or after the last stored version uses that version, with a warning. Attribute view is the view used and corrections the IDs of the corrections applied.

Corrections

sRtr corrects a few entries of SRTR's web dictionary that do not match the SAFs, each under a stable ID:

  • SRTR-DC-001: REC_COD in every TX dataset uses the format COD, not THCOD. The thoracic format THCOD is a subset of COD with the same meanings (COD prefixes their labels with "TH:"), and liver recipients' causes of death are COD codes that THCOD lacks. This was checked on a real TX_LI file only; for other organs it is a generalization.

A correction is applied only when SRTR's entry still has the value sRtr expects; if SRTR has changed it, sRtr keeps SRTR's value and warns. Codes that appear in data but are in no format are not corrected: their meaning is not documented.

See also

load_srtr_file() and set_srtr_wd(), which take a release.

Examples

current <- srtr_dictionary("2609")
attr(current, "snapshot")
#> [1] "2609-1"
head(srtr_dictionary("2609", table = "formats"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   Format   Code  Meaning                                                     
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>                                                       
#> 1 ABNLBRNC 1     1: No Bronchoscopy                                          
#> 2 ABNLBRNC 2     2: Bronchoscopy Results normal                              
#> 3 ABNLBRNC 3     3: Bronchoscopy Results, Abnormal-purulent secretions       
#> 4 ABNLBRNC 4     4: Bronchoscopy Results, Abnormal-aspiration of foreign body
#> 5 ABNLBRNC 5     5: Bronchoscopy Results, Abnormal-blood                     
#> 6 ABNLBRNC 6     6: Bronchoscopy Results, Abnormal-anatomy/other lesion
